claim_tested: TZF CCCH fingers read UAUU subsites through main-chain hydrogen bonds and aromatic stacking
key_finding: NMR structure of TIS11d TZF bound to 5'-UUAUUUAUU-3' (PDB 1RGO); two fingers bind adjacent UAUU subsites symmetrically; CX8CX5CX3H fingers with an 18-residue linker
context: Human ZFP36L2/TIS11d TZF domain, in vitro NMR
confidence_and_limitations: High. Reference structure for the whole mapping. Human protein, not a nematode TZF; no MEX-5 or MEX-6 structure exists with RNA bound

claim_tested: MEX-5 binds U-rich RNA with high affinity and low specificity; one residue per finger sets specificity
key_finding: Minimal MEX-5 site is six or more uridines in a 9-13 nt window; mutation of one amino acid per zinc finger confers TTP-like UUAUUUAUU specificity; the discriminator is variable in nematode TZF proteins and invariant in other metazoans
context: Recombinant C. elegans MEX-5 TZF, in vitro binding
confidence_and_limitations: High for MEX-5. The paper does not test MEX-6, so transfer to MEX-6 is the inference under evaluation

claim_tested: MEX-6 itself binds mRNA and acts on the same 3'UTR as MEX-5
key_finding: POS-1, MEX-3, SPN-4, MEX-5 and MEX-6 all bind directly to the zif-1 3'UTR in vitro; MEX-5 and MEX-6 together antagonise POS-1 repression of ZIF-1
context: C. elegans embryo, in vitro binding plus in vivo reporter
confidence_and_limitations: Moderate to high. Direct binding shown for MEX-6, but the binding-site footprint was mapped with MEX-5, not MEX-6; no consensus or Kd reported for MEX-6

claim_tested: MEX-5 and MEX-6 act redundantly on the same process
key_finding: Degradation of CCCH germ-plasm proteins in somatic cells is activated by the redundant CCCH finger proteins MEX-5 and MEX-6
context: C. elegans early embryo, RNAi and genetics
confidence_and_limitations: Moderate. Genetic redundancy is consistent with shared targets but does not prove shared RNA specificity

claim_tested: MEX-5 and MEX-6 act together on a specific maternal mRNA
key_finding: MEX-5 is required for era-1 mRNA asymmetry and MEX-5 with its partially redundant partner MEX-6 are needed to activate era-1 translation in anterior blastomeres
context: C. elegans one-cell to multicell embryo
confidence_and_limitations: Moderate. In vivo genetic requirement, no direct MEX-6 binding assay on era-1

claim_tested: MEX-5 and MEX-6 are not interchangeable in every respect
key_finding: MEX-5 and MEX-6 gradients are regulated differently; PLK-1 modulates the MEX-6 gradient through physical interaction with MEX-6 while acting on MEX-5 indirectly via cortical polarity
context: C. elegans zygote, live imaging and genetics
confidence_and_limitations: High for the gradient claim. The divergence is in protein-level regulation, not in RNA recognition

claim_tested: MEX-5 and MEX-6 are differently regulated and non-identical in dosage behaviour
key_finding: mex-5 single mutants are inviable with a Mex phenotype; POS-1 binds the mex-6 3'UTR and reducing pos-1 dosage suppresses mex-5(-)
confidence_and_limitations: Moderate. Shows regulatory asymmetry between the paralogs; silent on RNA-binding specificity

claim_tested: Nematode TZF paralogs can recognise divergent RNA elements
key_finding: The POS-1 recognition element is distinct from sequences recognised by related proteins from both mammals and nematodes
context: Recombinant C. elegans POS-1, in vitro
confidence_and_limitations: High. Shows that close TZF paralogs in C. elegans are not automatically equivalent, so shared specificity must be argued from the contact residues, not from homology alone

claim_tested: Features beyond the contact residues shape TZF specificity
key_finding: POS-1 TZF solution structure shows the domain interconverts between conformations and that correlated internal dynamics are needed for target recognition
context: Recombinant C. elegans POS-1 TZF, NMR
confidence_and_limitations: Moderate. Implies that a residue-identity argument alone cannot fully predict specificity for nematode TZF proteins

claim_tested: MEX-6 carries the MEX-5 RNA-reading surface
key_finding: 27 of 30 RNA-contacting positions derived from the 1RGO ensemble are identical between MEX-6 (Q09436) and MEX-5 (Q9XUB2), including Arg in ZF1 and Lys in ZF2 at the C1-2 discriminator where human TTP and TIS11d have invariant Glu; the 3 differences are all in ZF1 and are derived in C. elegans MEX-6 relative to 9 other Caenorhabditis family sequences
context: UniProt sequences, PDB 1RGO, AlphaFold DB v6 models
confidence_and_limitations: Moderate. Residue mapping is a prediction, not a binding measurement; the anchor-relative alignment assumes the MEX-5/MEX-6 CX9/CX10 knuckle insertions do not reposition the contacting residues, which is untested experimentally

claim_tested: The MEX-6 TZF fold matches the RNA-bound TIS11d finger geometry
key_finding: AlphaFold MEX-6 ZF1 and ZF2 superpose on 1RGO model 1 chain A at 0.38 and 0.39 A CA-RMSD over 17 anchor-matched CA atoms each; TZF window pLDDT 83.6 against 54.0 for the whole protein
confidence_and_limitations: Moderate. Individual-finger agreement is expected for a conserved fold; the tandem superposition (3.77 A) reflects apo linker geometry in the AlphaFold model and is not evidence about RNA binding

claim_tested: 27/30 is within the range seen between TZF proteins of identical measured specificity
key_finding: Pairs with a known shared element score 26-30/30 and share the discriminator pair (ZFP36L1 vs ZFP36L2 30/30, TTP human vs mouse 30/30, TTP vs ZFP36L2 26/30); pairs with a known different element score 17-18/30 and differ at the discriminator; MEX-5 vs MEX-6 is 27/30 with an identical discriminator pair
context: UniProt sequences mapped onto PDB 1RGO contacts
confidence_and_limitations: Moderate. Within the TZF block, contacting positions are not more conserved than non-contacting ones (90.0% vs 81.0%, Fisher p=0.341), so the inference rests on the calibration and on which positions differ, not on a conservation signal

claim_tested: The discriminator is the C1-2 position, assigned without access to the PMID 17264081 full text
key_finding: Of the 30 contacting positions, only C1-2 and C3+1 satisfy both 'MEX-5 differs from the invariant metazoan residue in each finger' and 'invariant in 15 metazoan, variable in 232 nematode TTP-family sequences'; C3+1 contacts uridines only (adenine contact frequency 0.00), while TIS11d E157 is the closest side chain to an adenine base of any position (median 2.92 A to A7, under 4 A in 20/20 models)
context: PDB 1RGO 20-model ensemble, UniProt and InterPro IPR000571 sequence sets
confidence_and_limitations: Moderate to high for finger 1. The finger-2 equivalent E195 lies a median 4.36 A from A3 and is under 4 A in only 2/20 models, so the finger-2 assignment is looser

claim_tested: The three MEX-6 substitutions resemble those found between same-specificity paralogs
key_finding: MEX-5 vs MEX-6: 3 differences, mean BLOSUM62 -0.33, none at the discriminator, and 2 of the 3 (ZF1 C1+2, ZF1 C2+1) at the same positions where human TTP differs from ZFP36L2 and ZFP36L1, which bind the same element; pairs with a measured different element differ at 12-13 positions including the discriminator
context: BLOSUM62 weighted by base-contact frequency over the 1RGO ensemble
confidence_and_limitations: Moderate. All three differences are at positions that contact an RNA base in 20/20 models; substitution matrices do not model base readout directly

claim_tested: The predicted U-rich element is present in the one measured MEX-6 target
key_finding: The 304 nt zif-1 3'UTR (Ensembl F59B2.6.1) is 40.5% U and has 141 start positions matching the measured MEX-5 minimal element, covering 64% of the UTR, but a composition-matched shuffle gives 129.3 +/- 9.9, empirical p = 0.119
confidence_and_limitations: Moderate. Consistent with the prediction but not discriminating, because the element arises from base composition alone, as PMID 17264081 states
